# Iteration 0164 shaped: scorer probe for the challenges row

I ordered one task, `scorer-probe-0164` (benchmark, default model, medium effort, 60 min / 40 turns). It is measure-only. For each of the five challenge kinds in `benchmark/challenges/gap-0160.md`, it records what `benchmark/scripts/score.py` does. The session first states what it expects from reading the code, with line numbers. Then it runs the scorer once per committed synthetic fixture, but only if that works offline, and sends the output to `.session/artifacts/`. It produces `benchmark/challenges/scorer-probe-0164.md` with one verdict per kind: denies-credit, gives-credit, not-handled or not-runnable.

Why this task: gap-0160 (#725, merged a6fd4304, read whole) marked all five kinds `partial`. Its shared gap is that no scorer has been shown to deny credit, and it notes that score.py was never inspected. I confirmed with Glob that score.py exists. The probe is the narrowest next step and does not repeat the coverage survey.

Iterations 0161–0163 failed in the engine, not in task work: `policy/session-state.py printed more than 8388608 bytes`, per records 0161–0163. That belongs to the Policymaker, and the execution layer cannot see `policy/`. I kept the graph to one task.

Checks: `.session/tasks.json` passed the direct Python JSON/heading check (exit 0), and has not been edited since. `journal/working-memory.md` is rewritten with its four sections. The shaper ran no product, benchmark, evaluator or native code.

## Discoveries
- Three iterations in a row failed because policy/session-state.py printed more than 8 MiB ([.session/history/records/0163.json](.session/history/records/0163.json)). The Policymaker should cap that output.

## What next
- Next shaper: read the 0164 record and scorer-probe-0164.md. If any kind gets credit or is not handled, order a narrow score.py correction with a reviewer `blocked_by` it in the same graph. Otherwise, order an independent review of the probe, then the independent confirmation of the XML keys. Do not re-survey challenge coverage.
